title: Lost in Another Dimension
hook: Predicting which passengers of the Spaceship Titanic were transported to another dimension, using logic-based imputation and a tuned CatBoost model

slides.title: Lost in Another Dimension
slides.subtitle: Kaggle "Spaceship Titanic" competition
slides.narration: This is a Kaggle sci-fi twist on the classic Titanic problem. A spaceship hit a spacetime anomaly, and the task is to predict which passengers were transported to another dimension.

slides.title: The data
bullets: Passenger ID (with group), home planet, cabin, destination, age, VIP and cryosleep
Five onboard spending columns: room service, food court, mall, spa and VR deck
The classes are balanced, so accuracy is a fair metric
slides.narration: There are almost nine thousand passengers, split evenly between transported and not. Small gaps are scattered across nearly every column.

slides.title: Detective work on missing data
bullets: The cabin deck reveals the home planet: decks A, B, C and T are over 98% Europa, and deck G is 99.7% Earth
Passengers in cryosleep can't spend, so zero spending identifies missing cryosleep values
Passengers in the same group usually share a planet, deck and side, so groups fill each other's gaps
Age was filled with the median for each home planet and cryosleep combination
slides.narration: Instead of filling gaps with averages, Divyesh used the data's own rules. For example, people in cryosleep can't spend money, and certain decks only hold passengers from one planet.

slides.title: The pipeline

steps.label: Engineer
steps.detail: 24 features: deck, cabin number and side; log-scaled luxury and basic spending; group and family size

steps.label: No leakage
steps.detail: Group features are computed from training data only, and preprocessing is refit inside every CV fold

steps.label: Compare
steps.detail: XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost compared with 5-fold stratified cross-validation

slides.narration: The work moved step by step: build meaningful features, keep the validation honest, compare three boosting models, then tune the winner.

slides.title: Model comparison
slides.narration: All three boosting models were close, and CatBoost came out slightly ahead. Tuning it with Optuna added about half a percentage point.

slides.title: What predicts being transported
bullets: Passengers who were not transported spent more than twice as much on average (≈2,004 vs ≈886)
Where you slept on the ship mattered almost as much as what you spent
slides.narration: Luxury spending was the strongest clue by far, followed by where the passenger's cabin was. Big spenders were much less likely to be transported.

slides.title: What's next, and explore it yourself
bullets: Next: ensemble CatBoost, LightGBM and XGBoost for a final boost
Try the neural network that's set up but not yet trained
Biggest lesson: understanding the data's own rules beat generic imputation
